card.kicker: Arm AI Optimization Challenge 2026 · Cloud AI
card.title: NightShift
card.subtitle: Trillion-parameter AI engineers that run entirely on Arm CPUs. No GPU on Earth involved.

card.title: Frontier AI is assumed to need GPU clusters
card.subtitle: A trillion-parameter model usually means racks of expensive GPUs. I asked: does it have to?

card.title: Mixture-of-experts changes the math
card.subtitle: Kimi K2 has 1.04T parameters — but activates only 32B per token. Compute is small; the model just has to FIT IN MEMORY. And memory is what Arm cloud CPUs have, cheaply.

card.title: One Azure Cobalt 100 VM
card.subtitle: 96 Arm Neoverse-N2 cores · 660 GiB RAM · zero GPUs · ~$1/hour on spot.

image.caption: 96 Arm cores. 660 GiB. nvidia-smi: command not found.

card.title: I ran Kimi K3 — 2.8 TRILLION params
card.subtitle: Five days after release, on CPU, on Arm, via llama.cpp PR #26185 + KleidiAI. To my knowledge, the first CPU inference of K3 on Arm silicon.

image.caption: Kimi K3 (2.8T) generating on Arm CPUs — 2.3 tok/s, no GPU.

card.kicker: So what can it actually do?
card.title: Real developer work — starting with shipping code
card.subtitle: I give Kimi a prompt, and it writes a service — then I install and run it on the same Arm VM.

term.title: nightshift@cobalt-100:~ — Arm CPU, no GPU
segments: ./devjob_build.sh   # Kimi builds a microservice on the Arm CPU
[1/4] writing the service on Arm CPU...  8.6 tok/s
# a working microservice, written AND served by AI on Arm. no GPU.

card.kicker: And it scales to a team
card.title: One VM, four developers at once
card.subtitle: Continuous batching lets the same box serve concurrent sessions. Next: four real jobs at once — you'll see each prompt, each result, and its tokens/sec.
